text:
maria: quick heads-up — our streaming latency histogram in the console shows a weird 200ms spike band that only appears when the new node-client canary is active. low sample counts for the tail buckets too. anyone else seeing this?
aj: yeah saw it this morning, assumed sampling noise. but the spike aligns with a flood of short-lived reconnects from that canary. suspect sampling + quota windows interaction. :thinking_face:
kevin: could be the metrics aggregator dropping high-frequency events due to per-route throttle. the ingest path has a 100rps soft-limit we added last quarter.
sre-bot: alert: route/old-streaming/region-eu observed reconnect-burst > 500 in 60s (auto-mitigated).
anne: attaching a quick repro I used — simple SSE client that reconnects every 200ms for 30s:
```
for i in $(seq 1 150); do
  curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/stream?route=old-streaming" &
  sleep 0.2
done
```
It reproduces the bucket spike locally against canary.
tyler: interesting. console telemetry groups latencies into buckets [0-50,50-100,100-200,200-500,500+]. The 200-500 bucket is getting a disproportionate share. If reconnects create many tiny requests, the aggregation window might count connection setup overhead.
maria: we also see drop in `sample_rate` reported at the same times (console metric `telemetry.sample_rate` goes from 1.0 -> 0.1). that would explain undercounted tokens but not why latency bucket jumps.
aj: two hypotheses: (1) sampling is decided before routing failover so some routed requests get sampled differently, (2) aggregator backpressure causes delayed timestamps — so setup latency shows up as 200-500ms.
kevin: logging shows a backlog on ingest-pipeline pod: `enqueue_latency=220ms` in logs around the spike. that map to the bucket. i'm leaning to aggregator backlog.
anne: if backlog is the cause, then the console should display `ingest.enqueue_latency` next to histogram. current dashboard only shows overall p95 which hides this pattern.
maria: agreed — UX ask: surface ingest queue metrics and add a toggle to show sample_rate overlaid on histogram so SREs can correlate sampling drops.
console-bot: new feature request created: #FR-1482 "overlay sample_rate + ingest_enqueue on streaming latency histogram" — assigned to eng-platform.
tyler: short-term mitigation: bump ingest pipeline replicas for canary routes during rollouts, and add client-side jitter to reconnect to avoid synchronized reconnect storms.
aj: also propose changing when sampling decision is taken: make it after route selection so route-specific throttles won't change sample behaviour. Worth a quick API/impl discussion.
kevin: agree. also adding a debug trace id on reconnects would help: `X-Debug-Trace: <uuid>` so we can follow a reconnect through routing -> ingest -> console.
maria: can someone spin a quick canary flash with +1 pipeline replica and client jitter? I can run the curl repro and report if histogram normalizes.
kevin: i'll do the replica bump now and add a short-term override on route `old-streaming`. will post when done.
(12:07) kevin: done — replicas +1 applied to ingest-pipeline for old-streaming route.
(12:09) anne: ran the repro, spike attenuated by ~80%. sample_rate stayed at 1.0. Looks like backlog was amplifying perceived latency.
maria: excellent. next steps: aj/kevin/tyler to draft proposal for sampling-after-routing + trace header; anne to spec dashboard changes; i'll file follow-up rollouts doc for canary jitter guidance. :thumbsup:
